name: King Tubby
hook: An electronics repairman who rebuilt his own mixing desk and, in doing so, invented the remix.

blurb.age7: King Tubby took songs apart and made the empty spaces into the music.
blurb.age13: Osbourne Ruddock repaired radios and ran a sound system in Kingston. He modified his mixing board so he could drop instruments in and out live and slam echo onto whatever was left. Instead of a song with singing, you got a version with the singing mostly gone and the drums, bass, and echo enormous. That idea, that a finished record is raw material you can rebuild, underlies almost all dance music and hip-hop.
blurb.adult: Tubby's innovation was as much electrical engineering as music. He built a custom high-pass filter into his MCI board and used spring reverb and tape delay as performance instruments rather than corrective effects. The economic driver matters: Jamaican sound systems needed exclusive material, and B-side versions were a cheap way to get it. Scarcity produced a form.

signatureTracks.title: Dub From The Roots
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The title track of an album built from his mixes of other producers' rhythms, and the clearest early document of his style.

signatureTracks.title: King Tubby Meets Rockers Uptown
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Augustus Pablo's melodica track dismantled and rebuilt as pure space and pressure.
